why: deliberate (done after careful thought) is a near-opposite of arbitrary; ambiguous in (f)
reliance (depending on others) is a near-opposite of autonomy (ant: dependence)
oversight is a near-opposite (failing to notice) and its other sense 'supervision' is a near-synonym
impose 'force a ... punishment on people' overlaps condemn's also-sense 'officially order a punishment' in (g)
plausible (likely to be true) is a near-opposite of dubious (open to doubt)
dubious 'probably not honest' is a near-opposite of candid (honest)
susceptible (easily harmed) is a near-opposite of resilient (ant: vulnerable)
consolidate 'make a position stronger and more secure' is an opposite of undermine (ant: strengthen)
undermine (weaken a principle/decision) is a near-opposite of uphold
defy 'refuse to obey a rule' is a direct opposite of adhere (ant: violate, disregard)
prevail (win) is a near-opposite of concede in its 'admit you have lost' sense
resentment (bitter anger toward someone) could be read as the opposite of affinity (ant: dislike)
affinity (feeling of connection) is a near-opposite of rift (break in a relationship)
credible (believable) is a near-opposite of absurd (ant: reasonable, sensible)

set.also: extra, and kept ready as a backup in case the main part fails (“the plane has redundant safety systems”)

why: old also-sense was British-only (spec excludes British-only usage; not common for American learners); replaced with the common American technical sense

set.def: a statement or situation that seems to say two opposite things at once, yet may still be true

why: plain-word rule: 'self-contradictory' is harder than the headword

set.def: enough for what is needed; to the degree that is required

why: plain-word rule: defined with 'adequate', a hard near-synonym
'support' is a forced opposite; backlash has no real antonym
'include' is not a true synonym: comprise means made up of all the parts, include can mean only some
